prompt: Design a distributed multi-tenant API Rate Limiting service capable of enforcing tiered request quotas (e.g., 10,000 req/min) across thousands of API gateway instances with sub-5ms latency.
clarifyingInfo: Must handle multi-region deployments, race conditions, and support headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After).
expectedPoints: Evaluate algorithms: Token Bucket vs Leaky Bucket vs Sliding Window Counter
Distributed cache architecture: Redis cluster with Lua scripts for atomic increments
Multi-region synchronization and latency trade-offs (local in-memory rate limiting with periodic sync)
Handling Redis node failure: Fail-open vs fail-closed security trade-offs
HTTP response contract: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header
commonMistakes: Using relational SQL queries per HTTP request
Ignoring concurrency race conditions between parallel gateway nodes
Not defining fail-open degradation
followUps: How do you handle clock drift across regions when using sliding window timestamps?

prompt: Design a scalable URL shortening service like Bitly that handles 500 million new URLs per month and 10 billion redirect clicks, including real-time click analytics dashboards.
clarifyingInfo: Read to write ratio is 20:1. Custom aliases are supported. URLs expire after 5 years.
expectedPoints: Capacity math: 10B reads/month = ~4,000 QPS average (12,000 peak); 6-character Base62 keys provide 56.8 billion combinations
Key generation service (KGS) with pre-allocated token ranges to prevent collision
Redirect status code trade-off: 301 Permanent Redirect (cached by browser, loses analytics) vs 302 Temporary (hits server every click)
Caching hot URLs in Redis (80-20 rule)
Asynchronous analytics pipeline via Kafka to ClickHouse or Druid
commonMistakes: Using auto-increment IDs directly without Base62 encoding
Synchronously writing click analytics to the primary database on the redirect path
followUps: How do you detect and block malicious phishing destination URLs before redirection?

prompt: Design a video ingestion and adaptive bitrate streaming platform like YouTube, supporting upload, distributed transcoding, and low-latency playback across global viewers.
clarifyingInfo: Support up to 4K resolution across mobile and desktop. Average video length is 10 minutes.
expectedPoints: Chunking video at keyframe boundaries (GOP - Group of Pictures) for parallel transcoding
Stateless worker fleet on Spot Instances with queue visibility timeouts for fault tolerance
Adaptive Bitrate Streaming protocols: HLS (.m3u8 manifests) and MPEG-DASH (.mpd)
Multi-tier CDN caching: edge points of presence caching popular segments
Storage tiering: hot multi-resolution segments on CDN/SSD, original master files in cold S3
commonMistakes: Transcoding entire video files monolithically on single machines
Not handling worker node preemption mid-encode
followUps: How would you implement live stream transcoding with sub-3-second glass-to-glass latency?

prompt: Design a high-throughput real-time Metrics and Monitoring platform (similar to Prometheus or Datadog) that ingests 1 million metric data points per second from cloud infrastructure.
clarifyingInfo: Metrics have format: {metric_name, tags, timestamp, value}. Retention is 90 days.
expectedPoints: Ingestion scale: 1M metrics/sec * 64 bytes = 64 MB/s ingress; buffer via Kafka
TSDB architecture: in-memory ring buffers, Gorilla delta-of-deltas timestamp compression and XOR float compression
Downsampling pipeline: roll up raw 10s data into 1m, 1h, and 1d aggregations over time
Mitigating metric cardinality explosion (capping unique tag combinations per tenant)
Efficient query execution using inverted index mapping tags to time series IDs
commonMistakes: Using traditional relational databases with B-Tree indexes for write-heavy telemetry
Failing to account for cardinality explosion caused by user IDs in tags
followUps: How do you alert on sudden anomalies across 100,000 distinct server streams in real time?

prompt: Design a distributed Job Scheduler and Task Execution engine capable of executing millions of scheduled cron tasks and ad-hoc delayed jobs with at-least-once delivery guarantees.
clarifyingInfo: Jobs have varying durations from 100ms to 2 hours. Support priorities, retries, and cancellation.
expectedPoints: Storage for scheduled jobs: distributed sorted set or partitioned database indexed by execution_timestamp
Leader election for master scheduler coordinator using Raft or Zookeeper
Worker poll/push model with heartbeat leases and visibility timeouts to detect hung workers
Idempotency tokens to ensure safe retries upon worker timeout
Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for repeatedly failing jobs
commonMistakes: Single point of failure in cron scheduling daemon
Not handling split-brain or duplicate execution during network partitions
followUps: How do you handle a thundering herd where 50,000 jobs are scheduled for exactly midnight?

prompt: Design a distributed, horizontally scalable Key-Value Store with high availability and tunable consistency, modeled after Amazon Dynamo or Apache Cassandra.
clarifyingInfo: Must support get(key) and put(key, value) across hundreds of commodity server nodes.
expectedPoints: Consistent Hashing ring with virtual nodes for uniform data distribution
Replication factor N with preference lists across availability zones
Tunable Quorum consensus: R + W > N ensures strong read-your-writes consistency
LSM-Tree storage engine: Write-Ahead Log (WAL), Memtable in memory, SSTables on disk with Bloom filters
Gossip protocol for decentralized failure detection and vector clocks for concurrent write conflicts
commonMistakes: Centralized master coordinator creating single point of failure
Ignoring read amplification on SSTables without Bloom filters
followUps: How does hinted handoff work when a replica node is temporarily unreachable?

prompt: Design a real-time Chat Messaging platform like WhatsApp or Slack, supporting 1-on-1 chats, group channels up to 10,000 members, and user online/offline presence.
clarifyingInfo: 50 million daily active users. Messages must be delivered in order with read receipts.
expectedPoints: Connection tier: WebSocket gateways maintaining persistent TCP connections
Session registry (Redis) mapping user_id to specific gateway server instance
Message broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ) for fan-out to group members
Message sequencing using monotonic 64-bit Snowflake IDs per conversation
Heartbeat ping-pong mechanism for presence status
commonMistakes: Long-polling instead of WebSockets for active chat
Broadcasting group messages to 10,000 members on the gateway process thread
followUps: How do you handle end-to-end encryption key exchange across multi-device sync?

prompt: Design a real-time Search Autocomplete / Typeahead suggestion system for an e-commerce platform that returns top 5 popular search queries within 20ms.
clarifyingInfo: 10 billion searches daily. Suggestions should update hourly based on trending search volumes.
expectedPoints: Data structure: Distributed Trie with nodes pre-storing top K search terms
In-memory Trie cluster partitioned by query prefix
Offline aggregation pipeline: MapReduce/Spark processing query search logs and generating serialized Trie snapshots
Multi-level caching: browser cache (Cache-Control), CDN edge, and Redis fronting Trie servers
Client-side debouncing (300ms) to avoid keystroke spam
commonMistakes: Querying SQL LIKE '%prefix%' on every keystroke
Traversing Trie downwards and sorting frequencies on live query path
followUps: How do you filter inappropriate or out-of-stock search terms in real-time?

prompt: Design a scalable Distributed Web Crawler that downloads and parses 1 billion web pages per month while respecting politeness policies and robots.txt.
clarifyingInfo: Avoid crawling duplicate content. Handle trap loops, broken links, and domain rate limits.
expectedPoints: URL Frontier architecture: FIFO queue with host-based politeness queues and delay intervals
Deduplication: Bloom filters and cryptographic document checksums (SimHash) to detect duplicate content
DNS resolution caching to avoid overwhelming root nameservers
Distributed worker architecture with S3 object storage for raw HTML snapshots
Robots.txt caching service
commonMistakes: Hammering single domains with concurrent requests violating politeness
Falling into infinite spider traps caused by dynamic calendar URLs
followUps: How do you prioritize crawling high-authority frequently updated news sites over static blogs?

prompt: Design a real-time geospatial location tracking and Ride Matching service like Uber or Lyft that matches riders with nearby available drivers in under 3 seconds.
clarifyingInfo: 1 million active drivers reporting GPS coordinates every 4 seconds. 500,000 ride requests per hour.
expectedPoints: Geospatial indexing: Google S2 geometry cells or Uber H3 hexagonal spatial indexes
Ingress pipeline: WebSocket/gRPC gateways receiving driver coordinate updates
In-memory driver location store (Redis Geospatial / memory grid) keyed by cell ID
Matching engine: Ring search expanding concentric spatial cells to find idle drivers
Distributed lock / atomic lease on driver acceptance to prevent double booking
commonMistakes: Writing raw GPS coordinate pings to relational database on every 4-second tick
Calculating Euclidean distance instead of haversine formula / routing graph
followUps: How do you calculate dynamic surge pricing based on real-time supply and demand ratios per cell?

prompt: Design a multi-channel Notification System capable of delivering push notifications, emails, and SMS alerts to 100 million users daily.
clarifyingInfo: Supports marketing blasts and critical transactional alerts (e.g. 2FA OTP). Third-party vendors: APNs, FCM, SendGrid, Twilio.
expectedPoints: Decoupled asynchronous architecture using message queues (Kafka)
Channel segregation: dedicated topics and worker pools for push, email, SMS
Priority queues: transactional OTP messages bypass bulk marketing campaign backlogs
Deduplication and idempotency keys to prevent duplicate sends
Rate limiting and opt-out user preference enforcement
commonMistakes: Calling third-party vendor APIs synchronously in client request path
No retry strategy or dead letter queue when vendor APIs fail
followUps: How do you track open rates and click-through rates across email campaigns?

prompt: Design a high-concurrency Flash Sale Inventory Reservation system where 100,000 users attempt to purchase 1,000 limited-edition items at the exact same second.
clarifyingInfo: Never oversell inventory. Unpaid reserved items must be returned to stock after a 10-minute timeout.
expectedPoints: Shielding database: In-memory atomic inventory deduction using Redis Lua scripts (DECRBY)
Virtual waiting room / token queue to gate traffic ingress at API gateway
Optimistic locking vs Redis distributed locks for inventory state
Delayed message queues (Kafka/RabbitMQ) to release inventory if order is not completed in 10 minutes
Async order creation: push successful reservations to order processing queue
commonMistakes: Direct SQL updates with table-locking transactions causing database deadlocks
Race conditions leading to overselling beyond stock limits
followUps: How do you defend against automated scalper bots and multi-account cart reservations?

prompt: Design a cloud storage and file synchronization service like Dropbox or Google Drive that synchronizes file edits across multiple devices efficiently.
clarifyingInfo: Files can be up to 50 GB. Support offline edits, version history, and delta sync.
expectedPoints: Chunk-based file transfer: divide files into 4MB chunks and hash them (SHA-256) for deduplication
Delta sync: upload and download only modified chunks, not entire files
Metadata database (Postgres/Cassandra) tracking file trees, chunks, and versions
Object storage (S3) for immutable chunk payloads
Notification service using WebSockets/long-polling to push file changes to connected client devices
commonMistakes: Uploading whole files on minor edits wasting user bandwidth
Lack of conflict resolution when two devices edit offline concurrently
followUps: How would you implement differential block compression (rsync algorithm)?

prompt: Design a collaborative real-time rich-text editing engine like Google Docs or Figma where multiple users can type simultaneously in the same document with zero conflict divergence.
clarifyingInfo: Must support offline editing with eventual consistency upon reconnecting. Up to 50 concurrent editors per document.
expectedPoints: Compare conflict resolution algorithms: Operational Transformation (OT) vs Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs)
WebSocket connection tier with centralized document session coordinator (for OT)
Character positioning via fractional indexing or unique operation IDs
Snapshotting and Write-Ahead Log to enable version history and fast document recovery
Presence cursor synchronization (ephemeral state over UDP or lightweight WebSockets)
commonMistakes: Naive last-write-wins (LWW) overwriting collaborator edits
Sending full document text on every keystroke
followUps: How do CRDTs handle memory bloat from tombstones of deleted characters?

prompt: Design a highly reliable Payment Gateway and Processing service (like Stripe) that handles credit card transactions with strict idempotency and zero double-charge risk.
clarifyingInfo: System must be PCI-DSS compliant. Third-party banking rails may experience transient network timeouts.
expectedPoints: Idempotency keys: Client submits unique Idempotency-Key header; server caches response in Redis/DB
Two-phase state machine: Authorize (holds funds) -> Capture (transfers funds)
Database transactions with strict ACID properties and audit ledgers (double-entry bookkeeping)
Handling ambiguous gateway timeouts: Automatic reconciliation jobs with banking partners
Tokenization service to isolate sensitive credit card numbers from application servers
commonMistakes: Retrying failed payment calls blindly without idempotency tokens
Floating-point currency math instead of integer cents
followUps: How do you maintain distributed consistency between your ledger and third-party bank settlement reports?

prompt: Design a Social Media News Feed generation system like Twitter or Facebook where users can publish posts and view an aggregated timeline of posts from people they follow.
clarifyingInfo: 300 million daily active users. Average user follows 200 people. Celebrities have 50 million followers.
expectedPoints: Fan-out on write (push model): write post directly into followers' timeline caches (Redis lists)
Fan-out on read (pull model): pull posts dynamically at read time for celebrity accounts (hybrid approach)
Timeline generation: merge K sorted lists of followed user posts
Feed ranking engine: ML scoring service re-ranking candidate feed items based on engagement probability
Media storage via CDN and asynchronous post publication pipeline
commonMistakes: Using pure fan-out on write for celebrity accounts causing millions of concurrent Redis writes
Querying relational database JOIN on every feed refresh
followUps: How do you ensure pagination remains stable as new posts arrive in real time?

prompt: Design a centralized API Gateway that acts as the single entry point for all client traffic across 200 backend microservices, handling routing, TLS termination, auth, and telemetry.
clarifyingInfo: Handles 100,000 QPS with p99 latency overhead < 5ms. Support canary routing and circuit breaking.
expectedPoints: Reverse proxy layer based on Envoy or NGINX with non-blocking event loops
Authentication and authorization: validate JWT signatures at the edge without querying auth service
Dynamic service discovery integration (Consul or Kubernetes DNS)
Resilience patterns: Circuit Breakers, retries with jitter, and bulkhead isolation
Distributed tracing: injecting W3C TraceContext headers (traceparent) into downstream requests
commonMistakes: Blocking synchronous I/O in the gateway filter chain
Cascading failures when downstream microservices timeout without circuit breaking
followUps: How do you route 5% of production traffic to a canary service instance by header?

prompt: Design a large-scale Distributed In-Memory Caching infrastructure to shield backend databases from traffic surges across 50,000 database read queries per second.
clarifyingInfo: Provide O(1) reads and writes, TTL expiration, eviction policies (LRU/LFU), and cache stampede protection.
expectedPoints: Consistent Hashing on client libraries to shard keys across cache nodes
Cache invalidation patterns: Cache-Aside vs Write-Through vs Write-Back
Preventing cache stampede / thundering herd (probabilistic early expiration or mutex locks on key miss)
Handling cache penetration (caching null values or Bloom filters for non-existent keys)
LRU eviction mechanics: Doubly linked list + hash table within each server memory pool
commonMistakes: Not setting TTLs leading to stale data indefinitely
All cache keys expiring at midnight simultaneously causing database crash
followUps: How do you safely resize the cache cluster without dropping hot items?

prompt: Design a centralized Distributed Log Aggregation and Search system capable of ingesting, indexing, and querying 50 TB of structured JSON application logs per day.
clarifyingInfo: Logs must be searchable within 10 seconds of emission. Support full-text substring and tag filtering.
expectedPoints: Log collectors (Fluentbit / Vector) buffering and batching logs on application hosts
Kafka ingestion buffer partitioned by application and service
Storage engine: Inverted index (Elasticsearch/Lucene) or column-oriented chunk index (Loki)
Hot-warm-cold storage lifecycle: SSD for hot 7-day logs; compress into Parquet/Zstd on S3 for cold storage
Log sampling and schema validation at ingestion gateway
commonMistakes: Indexing every arbitrary JSON field causing mapping explosion in Elasticsearch
Direct HTTP logging from app servers to indexers causing application threads to block
followUps: How would you execute distributed grep across cold compressed log files in S3?

prompt: Design a real-time Gaming Leaderboard service that maintains top 100 players and real-time rank lookups for 10 million active players across millions of score updates per hour.
clarifyingInfo: Support global rank lookup (e.g., 'You are ranked #1,402') and monthly rolling leaderboard resets.
expectedPoints: Redis Sorted Sets (ZSET) powered by Skip List and Hash Map: O(log N) updates and rank queries
Sharding high-traffic leaderboards by score ranges or geographical regions
Batching score updates via message queues to prevent write saturation
Historical archival of past season leaderboards in relational database
Handling tie-breakers (earlier timestamp gets higher rank)
commonMistakes: Running SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE score > user_score on SQL database per request
Not handling concurrent score updates correctly
followUps: How do you implement leaderboard rankings for friend circles with custom filters?
